spec_notes: ratchet/spec.md states every stated requirement (C-1 to C-52) and contradicts none. It marks as Open the handling of malformed or impossible FENs (C-3), the choice of standard positions and depths for move counts (C-50) and the benchmark protocol for the two time limits (C-51, C-52). It decides without marking: king captures never listed (C-17), castling needs king and rook on home squares whatever the rights field says (C-18), en passant needs the double-pushed pawn behind the target (C-20), the unsuffixed and wrong-suffix promotions are rejected (C-21, C-37), and the rights field is always written in KQkq order (C-31). C-53 to C-56 are marked as the builders' own discoveries. C-55 and C-56 (no conversion hooks called or even read for non-string moves) pin a choice a correct product need not share. C-51 and C-52 are written as Observables but nothing in the suite measures them.
tests_notes: Several tests cover many behaviours at once: 'the standard position has 20 sorted moves and 400 two-ply continuations' checks startFen, the exact sorted list and the depth-2 count; 'a saved FEN supports independent branches and resumes in a fresh process' checks branching, interleaving, a rejected move, a non-string move and a fresh process (it spawns a child node process, about 80 ms); 'missing and non-string moves throw IllegalMoveError without coercion' covers seven non-string kinds and conversion-hook call counts. Error-class assertions use assert.throws(fn, IllegalMoveError) with the imported binding, so removing the export makes them accept any error (S-17 break passed). No test passes an invalid FEN, and no test times legalMoves or the depth-2 count (a 100 ms slowdown per call passed). Tests that could fail on another correct build: rejecting 'a7a8Q' and 'e2e4q' (a build that documents accepting uppercase would fail), and requiring IllegalMoveError rather than TypeError for non-string moves plus zero conversion-hook calls. Nothing is tied to private functions or file names beyond the required src/chess.js. acceptance/*.cjs is not picked up by node --test.
maintainer: The move record shape ({from, to, promotion, victim, rookFrom, rookTo}) is shared implicitly by candidates, isLegal, boardAfter and remainingRights, and castling safety reuses boardAfter with a synthetic king move to test the crossing square, so a change to one of them can silently break castling or rights. remainingRights reads the pre-move board for corner rooks and king identity, which is easy to disturb. The two speed limits have no test, so a performance regression would pass npm test unnoticed.
